newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares edge higher in range-bound trade.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares edge higher in range-bound trade.

text.p: Istanbul shares saw modest gains in range-bound trade on Friday following a three-day down correction after the recent rally, brokers said.
The IMKB National-100 closed up four points, or 0.2 percent firmer at 2,010 after moving between 1,998 and 2,029. Over the week, it eased 0.8 percent after last week's 5.68 percent gain.
Daily volume rose to 25.83 trillion lira ($167 million), compared to Thursday's 20.78 trillion lira ($134.6 million).

"Demand for bluechip shares of state and energy firms remained weak, so the index was squeezed in a tight band. However the index's 2,000 level proved to be a firm support after today's test," Murat Turgut from BAB Securities said.
"Mid-year profit forecests of companies as well as government moves awaited next week also kept the market positive," he added.

The index slipped 1.8 percent in a down correction in the past three days after soaring 30.5 percent and hitting 10 records to Monday's all-time high close of 2,043 from June 18 when the former Islamist-led coalition government resigned.
A down correction had begun on Tuesday after the new coalition won a confidence vote in parliament last Saturday.
